en: *Yoginījālamahātantra*, Nepalese manuscript, Takaoka DH 377,
chapter 26 on the *ācārya* (with CP), page sequence uncertain.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the procedure for the Vajrācārya;
he who has mastered the scriptures is everywhere the bestower of fearlessness upon all.

Through the application of mantra and tantra, those who are skilled in the three collections of scriptures possess sweetness of speech toward all sentient beings, regarding them as their own children.
Always delighting in generosity and the other perfections, devoted to yoga, meditation, and so forth,
truthful in speech, non-violent, and possessing a mind of compassion and kindness;
The seal of the mind is indeed equanimity; for the sake of sentient beings who are without a protector, [he acts] as one truly become.
And according to the particular dispositions of sentient beings, he becomes a kinsman for those who are without a protector.
Possessing a beautiful form with senses and body fully perfected,
he was skilled in the true principles of consecration and an ocean of virtues expressed through clear speech.
The dialogue concerning the sacred seats (pīṭha) is always addressed to the teacher;
the teacher should accept the disciple who is of noble lineage, wealthy, and devoted to the dharma and its festivals.
He is undoubtedly merciless, wrathful, cruel, and tormented; he is excessively talkative, harsh, and devoid of compassion toward living beings.
One should always avoid the property of others at night with a teacher who is steadfast,
humble-minded, wise, secure, and free from deceit in acquiring wealth.
Renouncing his own ten kinsmen, he was pleasing to behold for all beings;
he avoided touching the property of others as one would avoid blazing fire or poison.
They always perform the worship of the guru and the festival of seeing him constantly;
they are ever devoted to charity and other virtues, desiring the higher world.
Among those excellent disciples, one should initiate [the candidate] into the auspicious maṇḍala;
having joined his palms in reverence, he should make his request with a focused mind.
"You are my teacher, O Great Hero, the union of the best of Yoginīs.
O Great Lord, I desire the firm method of great awakening."
Grant me the samaya, and grant me the bodhicitta;
[grant it] for the sake of the Vīras and Vīreśvarīs, and for Vārāhī and Heruka.
Explain the purification of the secret seats and so forth as they reside within the body;
grant me the Triple Gem: the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
"O Great Lord, cause me to enter the supreme city of great liberation!
Come, child, to this firm system of the practice of mantras of the Mahāyāna."
I shall teach you correctly, O vessel of the Great Vehicle;
you have attained incomparable knowledge through the cultivation of the Vajra-mantras.
Therefore, my child, apply your mind to this for the sake of attaining omniscience:
reverence for the guru, as well as loving-kindness, devotion to the Buddha, and kindness toward people.
Having abandoned the root downfalls, one should avoid the gross downfalls;
one should practice the propitiation of reality, yet one may also follow the Hīnayāna.
Those who have not crossed over, I shall cause to cross; those who are not liberated, I shall liberate;
I shall comfort sentient beings from the ocean of suffering that is saṃsāra.
For him, the preliminary consecration (adhivāsana) is performed together with his disciples for the sake of the disciples;
then, out of compassion, he [administers] poison and wood, in accordance with the rules of purity and mindfulness.
Bound with a red thread, especially having her arms reddened,
one should cause him to offer [the oblation] while joined with the *dhīḥ* mantra.
One should bestow the restraint of body, speech, and mind, and examine the entire system of dreams, both auspicious and inauspicious.
While leading [the disciple] into the mandala where they stand behind the blindfold,
he should cause them to grasp a flower, together with the ritual fee (dakṣiṇā), while the light is revealed.
Having purified the sins of previous births and so forth by beholding the mandala, he asked, "Who are you? and [the other] replied, "I am Subhaga."
One should cast a flower upon the mandala at the junction of the path of water;
whichever tantra that flower falls upon, that will be one's family.
The water, crown, vajra, bell, and name consecrations constitute the [fivefold] consecration;
the remainder consists of the five Tathāgatas, while the rest is Brahman.
